maps.nature: Use case: illustration-story. Production background for a polished Chinese mobile emergency education game. ONE seamless very tall portrait world map, aspect ratio 1:3, high resolution. Painterly warm gouache and watercolor picture-book art, sophisticated architectural details, lush sage and olive trees, terracotta roofs, cream paths, readable saturated teal water, warm sunlight. Slight elevated isometric view; consistent scale throughout, NO horizon or perspective shrinkage. A winding ivory walking path ascends from the bottom to the top, weaving beside every landmark; comfortable clear paving for game node overlays beside landmarks. No UI, no badges, no flowers-as-markers, NO letters, labels, numbers or compass. Each landmark appears ONCE. All locations are connected organically by lanes, gardens and water; NOT panels, cards, or separated islands. Quiet safe surroundings; hazards and motion will be separate overlays. Exact placement below is important; percentages measure x from left and y from top. Keep landmarks within canvas, detailed and immediately identifiable. Natural disaster landscape with ELEVEN distinctly spaced locations: (x30%,y91%) a sturdy seaside villa with exposed balcony doors and wind-swept palms for typhoon preparation; (x72%,y83%) riverside emergency supply shed with shelves, bag and water barrels for flood kit; (x30%,y75%) cutaway apartment bedroom with bed and tall bookcase for earthquake hazard search; (x72%,y67%) street corner with lamp posts and sign for storm street hazards; (x27%,y59%) park lawn with lone tall tree and sheltered pavilion for lightning; (x71%,y51%) woodland picnic clearing with stone fire ring for forest fire prevention; (x27%,y43%) urban street storm drain and curb for rainy street preparation; (x73%,y35%) two-story river house with water at the doorstep for flood response; (x28%,y27%) cutaway living room with clearly visible sturdy wooden table and sofa for earthquake take-cover; (x72%,y19%) low apartment stair exit leading onto a wide open assembly square for post-quake evacuation; (x30%,y10%) taller riverside building with blue floodwater below and a DRY visible staircase leading up to a dry second-floor refuge terrace for flood high-ground rescue. A river meanders between right-side flood landmarks, dry routes connect all locations; no rescue people, no damage blocking dry stairs. Do NOT merge or omit these eleven places.
